description.short: One of Taiwan's premier 'High Mountain Oolongs' — crisp, creamy-floral, with a distinct cooling alpine sweetness
description.overview: The 'gao shan cha' (high mountain tea) category is considered the pinnacle of Taiwanese oolong craft — high elevation, dense fog, and diurnal temperature swings produce delicate leaves rich in amino acids.
description.taste: Silky, buttery, sweet, with very low astringency
description.aftertaste: Refreshing, sweet, with a lingering cool sensation in the throat
description.processing: Plucking → withering → light tossing → fixation → ball rolling → minimal drying without heavy baking

history.origin: Commercial tea growing on Ali Shan developed in the mid-to-late 20th century as high-altitude infrastructure expanded through central Taiwan.
history.development: The term 'gao shan cha' became a world-renowned quality benchmark largely due to regions like Ali Shan proving the extraordinary virtues of high-altitude cloud terroir.
history.modern: Today Ali Shan is among Taiwan's most celebrated tea brands worldwide, intimately connected to alpine tourism, scenic sunrises above cloud seas, and the historic forest train.
interestingFacts: Ali Shan is world-famous for its historic narrow-gauge mountain railway (Alishan Forest Railway), built during the Japanese era for logging and now carrying travelers past scenic tea terraces.
In Taiwan, 'High Mountain Oolong' is an official regulatory category requiring plantations to sit at or above 1,000 meters in altitude.
